your_book:
Jaleel's book closed Friday, July 31 with a modest unrealized gain of $247 on a $23,123 account (+1.08%), a respectable result for a capital-preservation mandate. The day's headline mover was NBIX (Neurocrine Biosciences), which cratered 10.08% — by far the worst single-day print in the book — trimming its position to $333.60 despite sitting on a 2.3% overall gain. That kind of single-session drop on a STRONG BUY rated name demands immediate explanation. On the positive side, NVDA led gainers at +2.93%, ZTS added +1.66%, BSX rose +1.59%, and SAP gained +1.51%, all benefiting from a software/quality rotation day. NOW (+1.05%) and ADBE (+1.01%) rode the same software-sector tailwind tied to Microsoft earnings optimism and rotation out of hardware names.

The drift problem in this book remains RKLB: at 14% of the portfolio — the single largest weight — it carries an AVOID verdict, a QARP of just 45.9, and is sitting on a -17.1% loss ($3,247 value). Price and thesis have been diverging for some time, and size is making it worse. LULU is a secondary drift concern: a guidance-cut risk flag, -7.0% overall, and comps deteriorating for five straight quarters, yet it still occupies a 4.6% slot. BSX (-2.4% overall, guidance slashed to 7–8.5% growth) and SPGI (-4.4% overall) are also underwater despite constructive verdicts.

Watch the pharma cluster into next week: the drug-pricing policy flag on GILD, NVS, NBIX, and VRTX has a noted next event of August 4 — just days away. NVS dropped 1.45% today, GILD fell 0.82%, and NBIX's 10% single-day drop may be pricing in something in that policy pipeline. ABT flatlined at +0.09% despite its STRONG BUY rating, suggesting the market is still digesting the EPS guide trim.

attention.headline: 10% single-session drop on a STRONG BUY name
attention.note: A -10.08% day with no headline context provided is an immediate red flag — Jaleel needs to identify the catalyst before the next session and decide whether the thesis holds or the position should be reduced.

attention.headline: Drug-pricing policy event due August 4
attention.note: The MFN pricing/tariff overhang flags across the pharma cluster have a next catalyst in four days; with NBIX already down 10% today, the cluster warrants close monitoring heading into that date.

attention.note: Five straight quarters of negative Americas comps, tariff margin pressure, and a stalled China business make the 4.6% weight hard to justify unless the Sep 2 earnings report shows a credible inflection.
